name: Universal Jukebox: Turntable
subtitle: Your music on vinyl, tape & CD
promotionalText: Play the music already on your phone on a turntable, Walkman, CD player or jukebox, with the words turning round the record. No account, and nothing uploaded.
description:
Your records are already on your phone. Universal Jukebox puts them on a turntable.

Choose a folder of MP3, M4A, FLAC or WAV files, or the songs synced to your iPhone's Music library, and Jukebox reads the tags, the covers and the lyrics inside them and files every album on its shelf. Tap one and the needle drops.

Pick what it plays on: a turntable, a portable CD player, a cassette Walkman, a reel-to-reel deck, a jukebox or a pocket player. Or let each album play on the machine of its year, so a 1979 record spins on vinyl and a 2003 one goes in the CD player.

The words go round the record
When your songs carry timed lyrics, the lines turn round the spinning record as they are sung, follow along in the lyrics panel, and can show on your lock screen. A lyrics file saved beside a song (Song.lrc next to Song.mp3) is read too, and you can add one to any song yourself.

Made for listening
• Crossfade and fades between songs, and Stable volume, which brings a loud track down to meet the rest.
• Shuffle, repeat, play next, and a queue you can see.
• A sleep timer that fades the music out.
• Lock-screen controls, and a choice of speaker or headphones.
• Artists, albums or tracks, in A–Z, random or genre order, as a grid, a list or a jukebox shelf.
• Shelves that play as playlists, and a list of the music you still want to get.

Yours, and only yours
Nothing is uploaded and there is no account to make. No ads, no tracking, no third-party analytics. To see it before adding your own music, try the example library: nine made-up records, made on your phone.

Universal Jukebox is open source (AGPL-3.0). The code is on GitHub: github.com/universal-simulation-ltd/Universal_Jukebox

Made in the UK by James Markey MBE and UNI·SIM.
